Confidence Score: 5/5

The pull request appears safe to merge; the added synchronization resolves the host-read readiness issue without introducing a new actionable defect.

Summary

This PR places eager, non-MXFP8 per-expert token counts in pinned CPU memory while retaining device-resident counts for graph and MXFP8 paths. - Synchronizes the current CUDA stream before returning host-resident counts from `ep_prepare()`. - Keeps MXFP8 counts on CUDA for device-side grouped-tensor construction. - Adds tests covering pinned eager counts and CUDA-resident MXFP8 counts.

Diagram

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[Construct EpBuffer] --> B{Graph mode or MXFP8?} B -->|Yes| C[Allocate tokens_per_expert on CUDA] B -->|No: eager non-MXFP8| D[Allocate tokens_per_expert in pinned CPU memory] C --> E[ep_prepare writes counts] D --> E E --> F{Counts on CPU?} F -->|Yes| G[Synchronize current CUDA stream] F -->|No| H[Return device counts] G --> I[Return host-readable counts] ``` Reviews (2) · Last reviewed commit: ["remove cutlass bump and add sync for sta..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/16a62c31d959db44b7f5e1d961e167258385421f)

**Host counts may be stale** In eager non-MXFP8 mode, `ep_prepare()` now returns a pinned CPU `tokens_per_expert` tensor while its CUDA writer remains asynchronous. A caller that immediately invokes `.tolist()`, `.sum()`, or another host read no longer gets the implicit synchronization provided by reading a CUDA tensor, so it can observe stale or uninitialized expert counts. The fused eager dispatch path synchronizes while sizing its outputs, but the standalone public `ep_prepare()` path does not. Please synchronize that path before exposing the host counts or preserve and document an explicit readiness contract.
